cases.title: Early MRE: ideal charge budget
cases.question: The documented batch used five amperes for eight hours. Compute the ideal four-electron O2 mass in g, assuming constant current; distinguish it from measured collected oxygen.

sources.facts: The abstract reports an eight-hour electrolysis batch at five amperes using iridium inert anodes. It does not provide a calibrated total oxygen mass for this batch.

cases.title: Scale-up objective versus achieved production
cases.question: The abstract establishes that the annual one-metric-ton oxygen production goal was achieved. Also express the stated GOAL as kg/h using a 365-day, 8760-hour year; do not call that a measured rate.

sources.facts: The abstract describes a scale-up effort toward a goal of one metric ton O2 per year. It reports experiments up to ten amperes and simulant loads of 500 g to 1 kg. It does not report achievement of that annual goal.

cases.title: Anode candidate: computation versus qualification
cases.question: The reported alloy-screening results were established by completed MRE experimental demonstrations rather than first-principles calculations.

sources.facts: The abstract describes first-principles thermodynamic calculations for refractory/platinum-group alloy screening in the presence of Fe and Si. Its final sentence calls for experimental demonstrations of the alloys in an MRE environment. It gives no measured 500-hour alloy lifetime.

cases.title: Anode lifetime claim beyond available evidence
cases.question: A shortlisted alloy is established to survive 500 hours inside an MRE reactor.

cases.title: Plant-model integration interface
cases.question: The described MAIT framework uses MATLAB/Simulink to integrate subsystem models for the MRE plant.

sources.facts: The abstract describes a plant system model spanning excavation to product storage. MAIT integrates subsystem models in MATLAB/Simulink. Total mass, volume and power requirements were computed for plant iterations; these are system-model outputs, not reported operating-plant measurements.

cases.title: Plant requirements: computed versus measured
cases.question: The mass, volume and power requirements described in the abstract came from operating-plant measurements rather than system-model computations.
